title: Missing Dimensions: Integrating Human and Social Systems into Digital Twin Engineering
abstract: arXiv:2609.12131v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Digital twins (DTs) have emerged as a key technology at the core of digital transformation, yet their engineering practice remains too narrowly focused on engineered and natural systems. This paper argues that four system dimensions must be explicitly recognized in DT engineering: Engineered, Natural/Biological, Human, and Social. Each dimension brings distinct properties, modeling requirements, and ethical obligations that fundamentally shape what a DT must represent and how it must be built. We further argue that as DTs extend into the Human and Social dimensions, the emphasis should shift from automated control toward decision support and occupant empowerment. We illustrate our arguments using a smart building as a running example and identify four open research challenges for multi-dimensional DT engineering.

translated_title: 缺失的维度：将人类与社会系统集成到数字孪生工程中
translated_abstract: 数字孪生（DTs）已成为数字化转型的核心技术，然而其工程实践仍然过于狭窄地聚焦于工程系统和自然系统。本文认为，数字孪生工程必须明确认识四个系统维度：工程系统、自然/生物系统、人类系统和社会系统。每个维度都带来独特的属性、建模需求和伦理义务，这些从根本上决定了数字孪生必须表征什么以及必须如何构建。我们进一步论证，随着数字孪生向人类和社会维度扩展，其重点应从自动化控制转向决策支持和用户赋能。我们以智能建筑为例阐述上述论点，并识别出多维数字孪生工程的四个开放性研究挑战。
tldr: 论文提出数字孪生工程应明确纳入工程、自然/生物、人类和社会四个系统维度，并主张随着数字孪生向人类与社会维度扩展，其重心应从自动化控制转向决策支持与用户赋能。
